question: Where is the Datum Plane (DP) located relative to the root rib on the stub wing?

options.text: 2.196 m (86.46 in) forward of the most forward point of the root rib
2.196 m (86.46 in) aft of the most forward point of the root rib
1.735 m (5 ft 8 in) forward of the root rib
At the most forward point of the root rib itself

explanation: AFM 6.2 defines the Datum Plane as 2.196 m (86.46 in) forward of the most forward point of the root rib on the stub wing.

question: How much engine oil is included when establishing the airplane's empty mass?

options.text: 2 x 7 liters, but only for the LH (critical) engine
2 x 7 liters (2 x 7.4 qts) — full operating quantity for both engines
2 x 5 liters, the minimum quantity per engine
No oil is included; empty mass excludes all consumables

explanation: AFM 6.3 lists full operating fluids, including 2 x 7 liters of engine oil (one engine's full 7.0-liter maximum, times two), among the conditions for establishing empty mass.

question: How much unusable fuel in the main tanks is included in the empty mass calculation?

options.text: 2 x 13.2 US gal (2 x 50 liters)
No unusable fuel is included in empty mass
2 x 1 US gal (2 x 3.79 liters)
2 x 0.5 US gal (2 x 1.89 liters)

explanation: AFM 6.3 includes 2 x 1 US gal of unusable main-tank fuel (plus 2 x 0.5 US gal unusable auxiliary-tank fuel if installed) in the empty mass condition.

question: What is the lever arm (moment arm) for occupants on the front seats?

options.text: 3.25 m (128.0 in) aft of the Datum Plane
2.63 m (103.5 in) aft of the Datum Plane
1.00 m (39.4 in) aft of the Datum Plane
2.30 m (90.6 in) aft of the Datum Plane

explanation: AFM 6.4.1 gives 2.30 m for front-seat occupants and 3.25 m for rear-seat occupants.

question: What is the lever arm for fuel in the main tanks?

options.text: 2.63 m (103.5 in) aft of the Datum Plane
3.20 m (126.0 in) aft of the Datum Plane
2.30 m (90.6 in) aft of the Datum Plane
0.60 m (23.6 in) aft of the Datum Plane

explanation: AFM 6.4.1: main tank fuel has a 2.63 m arm, versus 3.20 m for auxiliary tank fuel (if installed).

question: What is the lever arm for fuel in the auxiliary tanks, if installed?

options.text: 3.89 m (153.1 in) aft of the Datum Plane
3.20 m (126.0 in) aft of the Datum Plane
2.63 m (103.5 in) aft of the Datum Plane
4.52 m (178.0 in) aft of the Datum Plane

explanation: AFM 6.4.1: auxiliary tank fuel has a 3.20 m arm, further aft than the 2.63 m arm for main tank fuel.

question: What is the lever arm for standard baggage in the cabin compartment (behind the rear seats)?

options.text: 4.54 m (178.7 in) aft of the Datum Plane
2.30 m (90.6 in) aft of the Datum Plane
3.89 m (153.1 in) aft of the Datum Plane
0.60 m (23.6 in) aft of the Datum Plane

explanation: AFM 6.4.1: the standard cabin baggage compartment has a 3.89 m arm; the nose compartment is much shorter, at 0.60 m; the baggage extension is 4.54 m.

question: What is the lever arm for baggage in the nose compartment?

options.text: 3.89 m (153.1 in) aft of the Datum Plane
2.196 m (86.46 in) aft of the Datum Plane
1.00 m (39.4 in) aft of the Datum Plane
0.60 m (23.6 in) aft of the Datum Plane

explanation: AFM 6.4.1: the nose baggage compartment has a short 0.60 m arm, being close to the front of the airplane relative to the Datum Plane.

question: How can a pilot verify that an installed auxiliary fuel tank is truly empty before flight?

options.text: Set ELECT. MASTER and the AUX PUMP switch ON and check for the L/R AUX FUEL E caution on the PFD
Weigh the airplane on portable scales before every flight
Visually inspect the tank through the wing skin with a flashlight
There is no way to verify; auxiliary tanks are assumed always full

explanation: AFM 6.4 explains that setting ELECT. MASTER and AUX PUMP ON and observing the L/R AUX FUEL E caution confirms an auxiliary tank is empty.
